Features

Every feature you need to run LinkedIn outreach safely across many accounts

Connectora covers the full outreach loop: find leads, send connection requests and follow-ups from several LinkedIn accounts, pace every action safely, and handle every reply in one place. Here is everything it does.

Overview

What features does Connectora include?

Connectora includes a sequence builder, multi-account sending with pooled limits, plan-ahead scheduling, per-account safety controls and warm-up, paced invite withdrawals, lead sourcing from files, Sales Navigator and LinkedIn posts, a unified inbox with AI reply drafts, campaign analytics, and signed webhooks to your CRM.

Campaigns

How does the Connectora sequence builder work?

A Connectora sequence starts with a LinkedIn connection request, with or without a personalised note, followed by wait steps and follow-up messages. You can personalise any step with variables from your lead file, preview it against a real lead, and edit the sequence while the campaign is running.

  • Connection request. Optional note of up to 300 characters, LinkedIn's own maximum.
  • Note-limit policy. LinkedIn caps how many personalised notes an account can send each month. Choose what happens when that cap is reached: send the invite without the note (default, keeps outreach moving) or hold the lead and keep retrying with the note.
  • Wait steps. Set in days and hours, up to 90 days. Follow-ups always stop if the lead replies.
  • Follow-up messages. Up to 1,900 characters each, with a live character count.
  • Variables from your file. {firstName}, {company} and every other column you upload become variables. Tokens are colour-coded: green when mapped to a column, red when not.
  • Live preview. Renders each message for your first lead. A missing value renders as blank, so a lead never receives a literal {firstName}.
  • Sensible default. New campaigns start with: connection request → wait 1 day → message → wait 3 days → message → wait 7 days → message.
  • Edit while running. Changes apply to steps that have not been sent yet. Leads already mid-sequence are re-aligned, not restarted.

Sources: LinkedIn Help: note character limits · LinkedIn Help: personalised invitation limits

Sender rotation

Can one campaign send from multiple LinkedIn accounts?

Yes. Each Connectora campaign can use any number of connected LinkedIn accounts as senders. Leads are spread across them in proportion to each account's remaining daily allowance, so no profile is drained first, and an account's daily limit is shared across every campaign it sends for.

  • Pooled capacity. An account set to 20 requests a day sends 20 in total, not 20 per campaign.
  • Sticky senders. Each lead is planned on one sender. If that account cannot send, the lead is re-planned rather than fired from a random other account.
  • No double contact. The same person is never contacted twice across campaigns. A duplicate is skipped with the note "Already contacted in campaign …".
Scheduling

What is plan-ahead scheduling?

Plan-ahead scheduling means Connectora gives every queued lead a concrete send date, time and sender before sending starts. The plan respects each account's limits, working hours and timezone plus the campaign's sending window, so you can see exactly when every invitation will go out and why some are waiting.

  • Campaign schedule: timezone, active days and a from/to sending window.
  • Account working hours: each LinkedIn account has its own hours and timezone. Sending happens only where the account's hours and the campaign window overlap.
  • Honest queue summary: for example "212 scheduled today · 257 later this week · 147 from next week (weekly LinkedIn invite limit)".
  • Soonest-first queue. The queued list is sorted by planned time, with the next invite time shown in the campaign's timezone.
  • Pause and resume without a burst. Resuming a paused campaign re-plans every lead from the current moment and respects what each account already sent today.
Safety

How does Connectora protect LinkedIn accounts?

Connectora protects accounts with a conservative default of 20 connection requests per account per day, a software-enforced ceiling, randomised delays, opt-in warm-up for new accounts, a per-account safety score, automatic pauses when LinkedIn signals a limit, and an instant freeze if LinkedIn asks for a security check.

ControlDefault or behaviour
Daily connection requests20 per account per day by default; adjustable up to a hard ceiling no setting can exceed
Weekly invitation ceilingTracked per account, Monday to Monday
Follow-up messages40 per account per day by default
TimingRandomised gaps between actions, only inside working hours
Warm-up (opt-in)5 → 10 → 15 per day, then the full limit after three weeks
Safety scoreBands from restricted to strong, with a suggested daily limit
LinkedIn limit reachedThat account pauses until its next sending window; leads are re-planned, not failed
Security check or restrictionThe account freezes until you reconnect it
Failed-attempt budgetRefused attempts count too, so an account can never retry in a loop

Invitations

How do automatic invite withdrawals work?

Connectora withdraws pending LinkedIn invitations as a slow, scheduled queue instead of a burst. You pick invitations by age, or switch on auto-withdraw with a threshold between 7 and 90 days. Withdrawals run oldest first, inside working hours, up to 25 per account per day by default, spaced minutes apart.

  • Manual mode: select by age bucket: older than 30 days, 14 to 30 days, 7 to 14 days, last 7 days, unknown age.
  • Auto mode: per account, opt-in. By default it only withdraws invitations Connectora sent, never ones you sent by hand.
  • Built-in caution: invitations of unknown age are never auto-withdrawn. Selecting 1,000 creates roughly a 40-day drip.
  • Why it matters: a large pile of ignored invitations can count against an account, and LinkedIn lists "invitations ignored or left pending" as a reason for invitation restrictions.

Source: LinkedIn Help: restricted from sending invitations

Accounts

How do I connect and manage LinkedIn accounts?

You connect each LinkedIn account through a secure hosted sign-in page, so Connectora never sees your password or cookies. Each account then shows its status, Premium, Sales Navigator or Recruiter badges, daily limit, working hours, warm-up setting and safety score. If an account needs re-authorising, you reconnect it in place without losing history.

  • Status at a glance: Connected, Connecting, Action needed, Re-auth needed, Disconnected, Stopped or Error.
  • Needs-attention bar: surfaces only what blocks sending, for example "hit LinkedIn's invite limit, resumes at 9:00".
  • Reconnect in place: keeps the account's limits, warm-up history and conversations.
  • Nothing silently deleted: removing an account or a campaign archives a full snapshot first.
Reporting

What reporting does Connectora provide?

Connectora reports a funnel for every campaign and for the whole workspace: connection requests sent, connected, replied, completed and failed. Acceptance rate is connected divided by sent; reply rate is replied divided by connected. Each lead also has a timeline showing exactly what happened and what comes next.

  • Clickable funnel cards filter the lead table to that stage.
  • Totals are recomputed from summed counts, never averaged across campaigns, and incomplete figures are labelled rather than shown as zero.
  • Lead timeline: connection request sent (with or without note, including the exact note text), accepted, every message delivered, replies, and any failure reason with its retry date.
  • Retry failed leads with one click. Leads inside LinkedIn's re-invite cooldown are skipped and the button shows the earliest retry date.
Integrations

Does Connectora integrate with my CRM?

Yes, through webhooks. Connectora sends a signed HTTPS request for every inbound LinkedIn reply to a URL you choose, such as a Zapier or Make webhook or your CRM's endpoint. The payload includes the conversation history, a link back to the thread, and a signature your system can verify.

  • One delivery per reply, even if the same message is detected twice.
  • Automatic retries with back-off for temporary failures.
  • Safe destinations only: internal and private network addresses are rejected.
